facts.statement: Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni was described by Ksepka and colleagues.
The type locality for Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni is the Green River Formation.
Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni was found in the United States.
Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni was found in the region of Wyoming.
Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni is classified as a stem-ibis.
Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni is represented by an articulated partial skeleton.
Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni possesses a sharply tapering beak tip, suggesting it may have foraged by prying mollusks from their shells.
Researchers suggest Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni likely had divergent foraging strategies from R. messelensis, possibly feeding in streams rather than near lake margins.
Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni is a species within the genus Rhynchaeites.

facts.statement: Rhynchaeites is an extinct genus of wading birds classified as a stem-group threshkiornithid.
facts.quote: Rhynchaeites (Greek for "beak fossil") is an extinct genus of wading bird, a stem-group threshkiornithid

facts.statement: Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni was described in 2026 based on a largely complete, articulated specimen from the Green River Formation.
facts.quote: In 2026, a largely complete, articulated Rhynchaeites specimen from the Green River Formation of the United States was described as the holotype of a third species, R. mcfaddeni

facts.statement: The genus Rhynchaeites belongs to the family Threskiornithidae.
The genus Rhynchaeites belongs to the subfamily Rhynchaeitinae.
It is debated whether the parrot relative Mopsitta tanta is actually a member of the genus Rhynchaeites.
facts.quote: It has been hypothesized that the supposed parrot relative Mopsitta tanta, known from a single humerus bone, is the same bird as the leg fossils and thus actually belongs in Rhynchaeites too
